newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Transfield joins U.S. bid for RAAF contract.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Transfield joins U.S. bid for RAAF contract.

text.p: Melbourne-based Transfield Defence Systems has linked up with Lockheed Martin Corp and Northrop Grumman Corp in a bid to supply airborne early warning systems (AEW) to the Royal Australian Air Force.
"With Transfield on our team, we believe we offer Australia the best solution in terms of AEW experience," Lockheed executive vice president Al Hansen said in a statement.
The Australian contract is expected to be worth roughly A$500 million for an initial order of at least four aircraft.
The Transfield/Lockheed/Northrop team has proposed Northrop's AN/APS-145 radar mounted in Lockheed's C-130J-30 Hercules military transport airframe.
"The C-130J-30 platform has greater mission endurance and less per-hour operating and maintenance costs than other options," Northrop said in a statement.
The company said their solution offered cost savings training, technical support, logistics and facilities because the Hercules aircraft were already part of the RAAF's fleet.
Transfield was named in September as the preferred tenderer for a major upgrade of the Australian army's armoured personnel carriers.
Other suppliers shortlisted by the Australian government for the RAAF AEW contract include Boeing Co and Raytheon Co.
